A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LEQ research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across the title change and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original LEQ experiments on AntMaze, D4RL MuJoCo and NeoRL, together with component ablations and hyperparameter studies.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds original visual-control experiments, further ablations, numerical estimator analyses and model-prediction examples.

M1.justification: The state-based LEQ algorithm is largely retained, but v2 adds a visual-input adaptation using DreamerV3 architectures and ensembled stochastic latent prediction, with the entropy bonus removed (Appendix A). This substantially extends the model and input representation. Algorithm 2 also adds the immediate reward to the printed FQE target; the PDFs do not establish whether this corrects the implementation or only its description.

E1.justification: v2 retains AntMaze, D4RL MuJoCo and NeoRL coverage and adds eight pixel-based V-D4RL tasks: walker_walk and cheetah_run with random, medium, medium_replay and medium_expert datasets. This introduces visual-observation control beyond v1's state-based evaluations.

E2.justification: AntMaze Table 1 adds TT, TAP and IQL-TD-MPC and removes BC, TD3+BC and MOPO. D4RL Table 3 replaces BC and TD3+BC with TT and TAP. New visual comparisons include DrQ+BC, ACRO, OfflineDV2, ROSMO and a DreamerV3 implementation of MOPO. Table 5 also adds AWR and direct-Q policy-update comparisons.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a visual evaluation setup using a 12M DreamerV3 model, unnormalized rewards and five-step imagination, plus a comparison against fifteen-step imagination. New controlled experiments include a stochastic policy with entropy coefficient 0.0003 and learned termination functions (Appendices A and D). The existing state-based training budgets and main evaluation metrics are retained.

E4.justification: New analyses isolate policy objectives, EMA regularization, real-data critic training, expectile weighting, pretraining, policy stochasticity, learned termination and visual rollout length. Figures 5, 7 and 8 add maze-failure cases, numerical investigations of estimator exceptions and video-prediction examples. The full MOBILE hyperparameter sweep and training-variance plots already existed in v1 and are relocated, not new analyses.

E5.justification: Five-seed mean-and-standard-deviation reporting remains for state-based experiments. v2 separately specifies three seeds and reports means and standard deviations for the new visual experiments (Table 4 and Appendix A). It does not establish an increase in runs for retained experiments or introduce confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Main state-based LEQ scores are retained, while v2 adds visual results, comparator scores and extensive ablation findings. Table 4 reports a V-D4RL LEQ total of 307.6. Added AntMaze totals for TT and TAP are 494.8 and 517.0 versus LEQ's 470.4, although LEQ leads on ultra tasks. The ablation reference changes medium-play from 58.8 ±33.0 to 50.2 ±39.9 and its total from 470.4 to 461.8; 50.2 already appeared at expectile 0.1 in v1 Table 11, so this is not established same-setting deterioration.

T1.justification: Appendix B replaces v1's unconditional contraction claim with separate lemmas for optimistic and pessimistic estimates and a conditional theorem. v2 explicitly acknowledges that correcting an underestimate can increase error and supplies a probability condition for the non-increasing-error guarantee. This substantially revises both the mathematical claim and its proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion broaden LEQ's claimed applicability to pixel-based control and add competitiveness with sequence-modeling approaches. v1 emphasizes long-horizon AntMaze success and state-based locomotion; v2 presents a method applicable across navigation, state-based control and visual control, with broader claims of performance across domains.

C2.justification: v2 explains medium-maze failures through world models predicting impossible wall crossings, replacing v1's less specific training-variance discussion. Its limitations section replaces the proposed future extension to visual inputs with measured dependence on ground-truth termination, including the 461.8-to-232.6 drop in Table 22. It also adds interpretations of stochastic-policy suppression, pretraining effects and visual prediction quality.

D1.justification: Appendix A adds visual-model architecture and pretraining details, task-specific expectiles, MOPO penalty settings, continuous-action ROSMO settings and additional runtimes. v2 newly identifies the JAX implementation, revises reported CPU resources from four to eight cores, and states that code and replication instructions accompany supplementary materials. That availability statement cannot be independently verified from the supplied PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 expands positioning against sequence-modeling and visual offline-RL approaches, adding relevant works such as TT, IQL-TD-MPC, OfflineDV2, ROSMO and ACRO. Section 2 adds a substantive distinction between IQL's upper-expectile approximation of action maximization and LEQ's lower-expectile treatment of uncertain model-generated returns.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, its abstract and framing are revised, several method explanations are streamlined, and the ablation narrative is reordered. Limitations becomes a separate section, ethics and reproducibility statements appear, and supplementary results are separated by purpose. The main section sequence and much existing exposition remain; most expansion comes from added scientific content.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the noisy-critic schematic with a Q-learning comparison figure and adds maze-failure diagrams, estimator heatmaps and video-prediction panels. Comparison and ablation tables are substantially restructured, with new visual and component-result tables. The existing training-variance plot and complete MOBILE sweep move into the main text, alongside a document-wide change to the ICLR layout.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the paper through visual-control evidence, targeted component and termination ablations, and a qualified theoretical guarantee replacing v1's overly broad unconditional claim. These changes improve understanding of applicability and failure conditions. New inconsistencies detract from precision, notably the expectile settings across Tables 13 and 17 and Figure 2's reversed weighting inequality relative to Equation 11, but they do not outweigh the substantial gains in evidence and qualification.
